works.title: Strategic identity signaling in heterogeneous networks
works.summary:
**No findings can be stated for this paper.** None of its body text is readable. The extracted text file `C:\Users\pgoff\Documents\research\_text\4ccf0cf0dfc7.txt` is 18 bytes of blank lines. A filename search of `_raw`, `annotations` and `_work` found no PDF or other copy of the source. The only thing on disk is the annotation file `C:\Users\pgoff\Documents\research\_annots\4ccf0cf0dfc7.json`. It holds 47 Ink highlights, dated 2026-06-01: 42 yellow and 5 green, on pages 1 and 2. Every highlight has empty `covered_text` and empty `content`. That file records where Paul marked the page and in what colour, but not what he marked.

The title "Strategic identity signaling in heterogeneous networks" is only a metadata hint. Nothing on disk confirms it, and the authors, year, venue and DOI are unknown. I could guess what such a paper might say, for example about members signalling group identity to mixed audiences, homophily, or cue-taking across party lines. Any such guess would invent content, and a bearing built on it would break the rule that every bearing cites a page and a specific claim. For that reason no bearings are given for any component, which is a valid answer here.

**Why it still matters.** Paul highlighted heavily on the first two pages, and green on page 2 is used sparingly, so he probably found the abstract and framing important. If the title is right, the closest components would be:
- the partisan cue factors in the cascade kernel (`cpf_pressure`, the cross-party `sqrt(bpf)` term)
- the persona channel
- the ACU speaker mode

These are pointers for re-reading, not findings. The paper cannot be related to the system until the PDF is found and its text is extracted again (with OCR if it is a scan). The green page-2 highlight areas should then be mapped to text.
